To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optical characteristics of some fluorine-containing poly(1, 3,4- oxadiazole- ether)s in the presence of SnO 2, NiO, and SnO 2/NiO nanocomposites were examined using steady-state UV-Visible absorption and fluorescence spectroscopic techniques.
The optical characteristics of some fluorine containing poly(1, 3, 4-oxadizole ether)s in presence of metal oxide nanoparticles were studied.
the optical characteristics of some fluorine-containing poly(1, 3, 4-oxadazoles) in the presence of metal oxide NPs was modified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optical properties of fluorinated poly(oxadiazole) derivatives in presence of Sn02, NiO and mixed-oxide SnO2/Nio NPs.
the study of the interaction of metal oxide nanoparticles and some fluorinated poly (1,3, 4-oxadazolyl-ether)s.
the optical properties of some fluorinated polymers in presence of metal oxides nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SnO2, and SnO2–NiO NPs have a strong influence on the electronic structure of polymers and the fluorescence intensity.
the investigated polymers have a good potential for applications in optoelectronic devices.
the optical properties of fluorinated poly(oxadiazole) polymers in presence of metal oxide NPs is mainly influenced by their surface properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solute-solvent interactions and the polymer-metal oxide NPs interactions are not the only factors that control the optical characteristics of polymers in presence of metal oxide NPs.
the presence of metal oxides NPs can be used as an efficient tool to modify the optical characteristics of some fluorine containing polymers.
fluorinated poly(oxadiazole) polymers can be used as a good candidate in the development of optical sensor for detection of metal oxide NPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical properties of the fluorinated poly(oxadiazole) derivatives can be modulated by the presence of metal oxide nanoparticles.
the optical properties of some fluorinated polymers were changed by presence of metal oxide NPs.
the optical properties of fluorinated poly(oxadiazole)-ether)s are strongly affected by the presence of SnO 2, NiO and Sn 0.5 Ni 0.5 O NPs in the polymer matrix.
